stemMd: A mayor says that because every department cut its own paper use by ten percent, the city's total paper use must have fallen by twenty percent when two departments are combined. The error is that the mayor

options.label: A
options.textMd: uses a necessary condition as a sufficient one.

options.label: C
options.textMd: confuses paper use with paper price.

options.label: D
options.textMd: assumes the departments use equal quantities of paper.

options.label: E
options.textMd: adds percentage reductions that apply to separate bases.

explanationMd: Let the initial amounts be any two quantities. Reducing each to ninety percent leaves their sum at ninety percent too. The combined reduction is ten percent, regardless of the departments' relative sizes.

distractorRationale.d: Even equal quantities would not make the combined reduction twenty percent.
distractorRationale.a: The error is arithmetic aggregation, not conditional reversal.
